idiom_name: `data class` with `val` properties and immutable collection types
implementation_notes: Kotlin's `data class` derives `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`/`copy`/`componentN` from the properties of the primary constructor, so the classic value class becomes a one-line declaration; `val` plus immutable collection types provide immutability and `copy(...)` gives the non-destructive update. Only primary-constructor properties participate in equality, and `copy()` is shallow, so a mutable list inside a data class still aliases between copies; `@JvmInline value class` (Kotlin 1.5) is the allocation-free realization of the same idea when the value has exactly one attribute.
pitfalls: `copy()` and the generated equals are shallow: a `MutableList` or `Array` property is shared between copies and compared by reference - use `List`/`Map` and copy defensively.
Properties declared outside the primary constructor are excluded from `equals`, `hashCode` and `copy`, so state that determines equality must be a constructor property.
The generated `copy`/`componentN` become public API: adding a property changes `copy`'s signature and breaks already-compiled callers (a data class is not ABI-stable).
